verified_reasoning.claim: Small resolution X is smooth, integral, projective and of dimension three
verified_reasoning.reason: The charts s != 0 and t != 0 in X={at=bs,ct=ds} are A1 times P2. Their intersection is nonempty; X is closed in P1 times P4. Closed points therefore have depth three over C.

verified_reasoning.claim: Exceptional locus C has codimension two and pi is an isomorphism outside C
verified_reasoning.reason: C=P1 times vertex. At any nonvertex rank-one matrix (a,b;c,d), a nonzero row determines [s:t] regularly on the corresponding coordinate chart.

verified_reasoning.claim: The 31 cubics have no common zero and induce an immersion away from the vertex
verified_reasoning.reason: Count is 1+10+20. At vertex z^3 is nonzero; elsewhere some x_i^3 is nonzero. On that chart, x_i^2*x_j/x_i^3 and z*x_i^2/x_i^3 recover all original affine coordinates; the coordinate-ring map is surjective.

verified_reasoning.claim: Every nonzero pulled-back hyperplane through f(C) is nonnormal along generic C
verified_reasoning.reason: In the two-dimensional regular local ring at generic C its equation is in m^2 and nonzero. The quotient has dimension one and embedding dimension two, hence is not regular and cannot be a Noetherian normal local ring. A zero equation instead gives the wrong section dimension.

verified_reasoning.claim: Counterexample meets all original stated 8.16 hypotheses and has a codimension-one bad parameter subset
verified_reasoning.reason: X is smooth geometrically integral and proper with closed-point depth three; f is unramified off codimension-two C. Hyperplanes through f(C) form a dual hyperplane and all fail the demanded conclusion.

verified_reasoning.claim: Veronese double-line counterexample satisfies old (b) but contradicts the conclusion
verified_reasoning.reason: The double line is singular, one-dimensional and topologically irreducible. The discriminant hypersurface is irreducible of dimension four; its general section is a union of distinct lines, while double lines form a smaller two-dimensional subset.

verified_reasoning.claim: Normal quadric-cone counterexample satisfies old (a) and the dual-defective branch of (b)
verified_reasoning.reason: The cone xz-y^2=0 over C is normal, with only a codimension-two singular vertex. The section x=0 is a double ruling line. The Gauss image is a conic in dual P3, while general hyperplanes through the vertex cut two distinct ruling lines.

verified_reasoning.claim: Strengthened 8.16 retains depth and the necessary geometric properties
verified_reasoning.reason: Only f is strengthened to globally unramified. Depth >=3, geometric normality, geometric integrality and properness remain explicit. S2 of the section is not inferred from normality alone.

verified_reasoning.claim: Strengthened 8.18 is a sufficient condition, not a claimed equivalence
verified_reasoning.reason: The statement explicitly restricts to normal X and requires geometrically integral sections in (a)/(b). The proof uses open geometrically integral-fibre locus U and excludes every codimension-one component of the closed bad locus.

verified_reasoning.claim: Passing from the open integral section to the full section in 8.18 is valid
verified_reasoning.reason: The full nonzero section is an effective Cartier divisor on normal X, hence S1; all components have dimension d-1 >=1 and cannot lie in finite T. The integral open section gives one generic component and generic reducedness; S1 rules out embedded associated points and nilpotents.

verified_reasoning.claim: Arbitrary quasi-coherent G gives the first canonical closed immersion
verified_reasoning.reason: Sym G surjects onto the Rees algebra, and the tautological kernel H maps to zero under u after pullback to the blowup.

verified_reasoning.claim: Locally Noetherian regular-sequence calculation identifies V(K) with the blowup
verified_reasoning.reason: At points above T, (a1,a2-a1*t2,...) is regular; local Noetherian permutability makes a1 a nonzerodivisor on C. Off T, invertibility of an a_i forces a1 invertible on the relevant zero-locus chart. The kernel of C -> A[J/a1] is a1-power torsion and therefore vanishes.

verified_reasoning.claim: The rank-two coordinate identification and uniqueness argument are valid
verified_reasoning.reason: [T1:T2]=[-mu:lambda] gives the incidence equation up to sign. The complement of the centre is schematically dense in the blowup, and the target is separated over X, so two X-isomorphisms agreeing there agree everywhere.
